items.question: My crew will leave a 1.5-inch edge drop-off inside the travel lanes on a road posted at exactly 45 mph. How often do the UNEVEN LANES signs have to be repeated through the drop-off area?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 2, 2.4 A) drop-offs <= 1.5 in: W8-11 every half mile where posted speed < 45 mph, every mile where >= 45 mph. 45 mph exactly is the boundary and falls on the 'every mile' side.

items.question: A drop-off deeper than 3 inches is within 8 feet of an open travel lane. The work is short-term stationary, the crew is working in the drop-off area and it will not stay overnight. What is the maximum length that can be protected with just drums or cones?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 2, 2.4 C) first bullet: drums or cones allowed only for short duration/short-term stationary work, short lengths (200 feet maximum), work in the drop-off area and not overnight.

items.question: We have a shoulder drop-off of exactly 3 inches located within 10 feet of the travelway. How often do the LOW SHOULDER signs have to be repeated along it?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 2, 'Drop-offs within 10 Feet of the Travelway' B) > 2 in and <= 3 in: drums or cones, W8-9 500 ft in advance and once every half mile. Exactly 3 in is the top of branch B (C starts above 3 in).

items.question: During periods when construction is inactive, how deep can a localized excavation (drop inlet, bore and jack pit) within 10 feet of the travelway get before it has to be shielded with traffic barrier?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 2, 2.4 F) Localized excavations: those which exceed 36" during inactivity get traffic barrier.

items.question: A pavement drop-off exactly 30 inches deep sits 20 feet from the travelway. What protection does the TMP Design Manual call for?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 2, 'Drop-offs 10 to 30 Feet from the Travelway' B) > 2 in and <= 30 in: drums or cones; C) > 30 in: barrier or 6:1 wedge. 30 in exactly is in B.

items.question: There is a fill slope of exactly 3:1 about 15 feet from the travelway. Does it need traffic barrier, or what treatment applies?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 2 Terrain hazards >= 10 ft: non-recoverable slopes (3:1 and 4:1) get drums or cones; only critical slopes steeper than 3:1 need traffic barrier. 3:1 exactly is non-recoverable.

items.question: How far behind the curb face should concrete barrier be placed next to a curb?
items.note: Missing variable: where the work is. TMP Part 2 Ch. 2 D) Curbs: maximum of 9 inches behind curb face if work is in the travelway; minimum of 13 feet behind curb face if work is behind the curb. (Ch. 5 p45, an excluded page, has a different 12 ft rule for vaulting; not used.)

items.question: When an entrance ramp stays open in a work zone, how long should a temporary acceleration lane be to count as sufficient length?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 7, 7.3: temporary acceleration lanes of sufficient length (400'+/- - 75% of existing acceleration lane or whichever is greater) or matching existing length. The +/- is part of the value.

items.question: NCDOT's Work Zone Speed Limit Reduction guideline (not the $250 fine guideline) covers freeways whose existing speed limit is at least what?
items.note: TMP 8.3.2 Standard Practice for Work Zone Speed Limit Guidelines: freeways with existing speed limits of 65 MPH and above. Near-identical to 8.3.4 ($250 fine, 60 MPH and above, p86).

items.question: The NCDOT standard practice for $250 work zone speeding fines applies to roadways with existing speed limits of what and above?
items.note: TMP 8.3.4 Guidelines for $250 Speeding Fine Ordinances: existing speed limits of 60 MPH and above. Near-identical to 8.3.2 (speed limit reduction, 65 MPH, p76).

items.question: A work zone meets every Section I warrant for the $250 speeding fine ordinance but none of the Section II warrants. How many Section III warrants must it meet to qualify?
items.note: TMP 8.3.4: all of Section I and at least 1 of Section II; if Section II is not met, at least 2 warrants in Section III; if Section I is not met, it does not qualify.

items.question: Our work zone on a 65 mph interstate is exactly 1 mile long and will last four months. Does it meet the length warrant in Section I of the $250 fine ordinance criteria?
items.note: Section I warrant 2: the work zone is greater than 1 mile in length. Exactly 1 mile does not meet it (right answer: no, it must be greater than 1 mile).

items.question: Under the state law behind the $250 work zone speeding penalty, where do the penalty signs have to be posted for the extra penalty to apply?
items.note: TMP 8.3.4 Section IV quotes G.S. 20-141(j2): signs posted at the beginning and end of any segment of the highway work zone. Same statute text in tmsd L18_TSLG_Guide.pdf p285.

items.question: In the TMP Design Manual's positive protection chapter, where does the clear zone start?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 5, 5.2 Clear Zone definition. Near-identical definition in utilities if03014.pdf p91 and tmsd C34 - Manual 2012.pdf p101.

items.question: What truck weight and impact angle does the NCHRP 350 Test Level 4 crash test use, as defined in the TMP manual?
items.note: TMP Part 2 Ch. 5, 5.2 definitions: TL-4 = 17,650 lb truck at 15 degrees, 50 mph.

items.question: Under 23 CFR 630 Subpart J, the old rule required an annual process review of selected projects. How often do agencies have to do process reviews under the updated rule?
items.note: rule_guide 2.2.2 Process Reviews: former Rule annual; updated Rule changed to bi-annual reviews (the guide's word; the rule itself says at least every two years).

items.question: Under the former work zone rule the State designated a 'qualified person' to oversee the traffic control plan. Under the updated rule, who has to designate the project-level responsible person, and what must that person be?
items.note: rule_guide 2.2.3 Responsible Person: former Rule = State designates a qualified person; updated Rule = the agency and the contractor both designate a trained person.

items.question: The former work zone rule only had crash data analyzed to fix deficiencies on projects. What other kind of data does the updated rule add to work zone data?
items.note: rule_guide 2.2.2 Work Zone Data: updated Rule expands work zone data to include mobility/operational data in addition to safety/crash data.

items.question: NCHRP 350 used to be the crash testing standard for NCDOT work zone devices. Which crash testing requirements has NCDOT started implementing in its place?
items.note: 2023 Process Review, New Practices: starting to implement the new MASH crash testing requirements which replaced the NCHRP 350 requirements. (The TMP manual, 2019, still defines NCHRP 350 test levels.)

items.question: What passing grade is required on the written test of an NCDOT-approved Flagger course?
items.note: NCDOT Final Rule Implementation, Qualified Work Zone Flagger: passing grade of 70 or better (the Installer paragraph on the same page also says 70; the near-identical Designer paragraph, p5, says 80). No printed folio.

items.question: What passing grade does the written test for the NCDOT Work Zone Designer course require?
items.note: NCDOT Final Rule Implementation, Qualified Work Zone Designer (New - Proposed): passing grade of 80 or better. Near-identical to the Flagger/Installer paragraphs (70). No printed folio.

items.question: A town of 30,000 people has state roads with speed limits under 55 mph. What level of work zone training must at least one of its employees have?
items.note: NCDOT Final Rule Implementation, local governments: cities/towns under 50,000 population and state roads with speed limit < 55 mph need at least one employee trained to the basic level of ITRE's program.

items.question: When does NCDOT's Qualified Work Zone Designer training requirement take effect?
items.note: NCDOTFinalRuleImplementation p5 gives 'Proposed implementation date: 20??' (no date). Checked: no wztc document gives an implementation date for the Work Zone Designer qualification.

items.question: When an existing fire hydrant has to be removed for a project, within what distance of the main does the hydrant valve have to be for you to close it, plug its outlet side and pull the valve box?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf

items.note: Standard Specifications 1530-3(D) Remove Fire Hydrant. Same rule in utilities UAM (20220713 NCDOT UAM Ver 2-0.pdf p142). Printed page 15-17.

items.question: Per MUTCD Part 6, the LOW SHOULDER (W8-9) sign is for a shoulder elevation difference up to what?
items.note: MUTCD 6H.26: LOW SHOULDER for an elevation difference of 3 inches or less. Same text in tmsd Chapter2c.pdf p29 (MUTCD Part 2, 2C.29).

items.question: In a temporary traffic control zone, if a transverse rumble strip across a travel lane is not the pavement color, what colors may it be?
items.note: MUTCD 6M.06 P04: white, black, or orange. The near-identical Part 3 rule (tmsd part3.pdf p106) allows only black or white; the TTC rule adds orange.

items.question: In FHWA's work zone road user cost guide glossary, what is a faster-moving line of vehicles called?
items.note: fhwahop12005 glossary 'Queue' (printed 188). Near-identical definition in tmsd fhwa_hop_08_024.pdf p21.

items.question: For the MUTCG channelizing device taper notes, which formula gives the minimum taper length when the posted speed is exactly 40 mph?
items.note: MUTCG Ch. 2, 2.3 Notes for 'L' Distance (image-only page): 40 MPH or Less L = W x S^2 / 60; 45 MPH or Greater L = W x S. 40 mph is in the first branch; the divisor 60 marks it. Value read from OCR; page has no text layer.

items.question: List all the exposure control measures that 23 CFR 630.1108(b) gives as examples for avoiding or minimizing worker exposure to traffic.
items.note: 23 CFR 630.1108(b) Exposure Control Measures, 7 items in a two-column page: (1)-(4) on PDF p13 (printed 257), (5) rolling road blocks, (6) night/off-peak work, (7) accelerated construction techniques on p14 (printed 258).

items.question: When designing a temporary pedestrian pathway through a work zone, what are all the considerations MUTCD Part 6 (Section 6C.02) says should be addressed?

all_of: width of the existing pedestrian facility

items.note: MUTCD 6C.02 P11 list A-G: A continuity of accessible paths and B access to transit stops on PDF p14 (printed 778); C hard surface, D width / 60 in with passing space, E information for pedestrians with vision disabilities, F detectable edging, G signs below 7 ft not projecting more than 4 in on p15 (printed 779).

items.question: What are the steps of FHWA's process for requesting an exception for a significant Interstate project under the work zone rule?

all_of: submit it to the FHWA Division Office

items.note: rule_guide 5.4.1 Process for Requesting Exceptions: steps 1-3 (assess impacts; compare with policy; prepare and submit the request) on printed 5-8, steps 4-5 (FHWA reviews; take appropriate action) on printed 5-9.

items.question: In the Woodrow Wilson Bridge case study of FHWA's work zone impacts assessment guide, what information did the project web site contain? List everything.
items.note: wzi_guide Appendix A (printed A-10 / A-11): WWB project web site contents, 10 bullets: overall project, Bridge Bucks, Mission Possible (with sub-bullets) on p164; construction program, project news, neighborhood news, environmental aspects, civil rights/DBE, scrapbook, videos on p165.

items.question: FHWA's work zone impacts assessment guide gives examples of overall policy issues an agency's work zone guidance can address. List them all.
items.note: wzi_guide 3.x 'Examples of Overall Policy Issues', 8 dash items: standing multi-disciplinary team, agency organizational strategies, guidance on using the assessment guidance, MOUs with utility operators, performance levels on printed 3-13; significant-project criteria, exception criteria, training on printed 3-14.

items.question: Under 23 CFR 630, if right-of-way acquisition or construction for a road hasn't started after its federally funded preliminary engineering, by when must it start before the State DOT has to pay the Federal funds back?

expected.value: close of the tenth fiscal year

items.note: 23 CFR 630.112(c)(2), two-column page: not started by the close of the tenth fiscal year following the fiscal year in which the project is authorized -> repayment (extension possible). Same page as 'Subpart C [Reserved]'.

items.question: According to 23 CFR 630.1012, besides MUTCD Part 6, which document's work zone hardware recommendations must a TTC plan be consistent with?
items.note: 23 CFR 630.1012(b)(1), two-column page: consistent with MUTCD Part 6 and with the work zone hardware recommendations in Chapter 9 of the AASHTO Roadside Design Guide (2002).

items.question: If the PS&E uses method-based specifications, how can the TMP be paid for under 23 CFR 630.1012?
items.note: 23 CFR 630.1012(d)(1), two-column page: individual pay items, lump sum payment, or a combination thereof.

items.question: How does 23 CFR 630 Subpart K define Exposure Control Measures?

expected.value: eliminating or reducing traffic through the work zone

items.note: 23 CFR 630.1104 definitions, two-column page: traffic management strategies to avoid work zone crashes involving workers and motorized traffic by eliminating or reducing traffic through the work zone, or diverting traffic away from the work space.

items.question: How many responses did FHWA get to the docket for the supplemental proposed work zone safety and mobility rule, and how many of them were State DOTs?
items.note: Federal Register 69 FR 54562 (Sept. 9, 2004), three-column page 54563, Profile of Respondents: 33 responses, 27 State DOTs, 4 trade associations, 2 private individuals.

items.question: What does Subpart C of 23 CFR part 630 require?
items.note: 23 CFR 630 (2024 edition) p5 (printed 249) shows 'Subpart C [Reserved]': no content. Checked: no 'Subpart C' heading with a title in any wztc document.

items.question: What are the rules in Subparts E and F of 23 CFR 630?
items.note: 23 CFR 630 p6 (printed 250) shows 'Subparts E–F [Reserved]'. Checked: no titled Subpart E or F of part 630 in any wztc document.

items.question: What does section 630.707 of 23 CFR say about advance construction projects?
items.note: 23 CFR 630 p7 (printed 251) shows '§ 630.707 [Reserved]' between 630.705 and 630.709. Checked: '630.707' occurs only followed by [Reserved].

items.question: What does 23 CFR 630 Subpart I cover?
items.note: 23 CFR 630 p7 (printed 251) shows 'Subpart I [Reserved]'. Checked: no titled Subpart I of part 630 in any wztc document.

items.question: What assessment requirements do NCDOT's Work Zone Safety and Mobility Guidelines set during and after construction?
items.note: WZSafetyAndMobilityGuidelines p23: 'ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS DURING/AFTER CONSTRUCTION - To Be Developed' (placeholder, no content). Checked: the heading occurs nowhere else with content.

items.question: Under 23 CFR 630 Subpart G, when does FHWA start reimbursing a State for an advance construction project?

accept: converted to a regular Federal-aid project

items.note: 23 CFR 630.705(a)(2): FHWA shall not reimburse the State until the project is converted under 630.709. Live text on the page whose Subparts E-F are [Reserved]; 630.707 [Reserved] follows on p7. (The 'AC' project-number prefix in (b) was not used: a two-letter value would match almost any answer as a substring.)

items.question: Per NCDOT Roadway Standard Drawing 1101.11 (advance warning sign spacing chart), how far apart should the advance warning signs in a series be on a road posted at exactly 35 mph?
items.note: Division 11 Combined p40 (page rotated 270), RSD 1101.11 sheet 4 of 4, Advance Warning Sign Spacing Chart: row '<= 35' mph -> A, B and C all 200 ft. 35 is the top of the <= 35 row (40-50 gives 350). Drawings carry a drawing number, not a page folio.

items.question: On controlled access roads, what spacing does NCDOT's advance warning sign spacing chart (RSD 1101.11) give for distance C, between the 2nd and 3rd signs?
items.note: RSD 1101.11 sheet 4, chart header 'Recommended distance between signs (feet)+-' spans columns A, B, C; last row 'Controlled access roads (>= 55)': A 1000, B 1500, C 2700. Column C is also the distance to the 4th sign.

items.question: What is the minimum legibility distance for a Type B arrow board in MUTCD Figure 6L-3?
items.note: MUTCD Figure 6L-3 Advance Warning Arrow Board Display Specifications: Type B 60 x 30 in, 3/4 mile, 13 elements.

items.question: For a Type D arrow board in MUTCD Figure 6L-3, which has no minimum board size, how long must the arrow be?
items.note: Figure 6L-3 row D: minimum size 'None*'; footnote *: length of arrow equals 48 inches, width of arrowhead equals 24 inches. The answer is only in the footnote.

items.question: How long should a shoulder taper be, as a fraction of the taper length L, under MUTCD Part 6?
items.note: MUTCD 6B.08 P13 (PDF p12, printed 776): shoulder tapers approximately 1/3 L, printed with a superscript fraction glyph. Table 6B-3 on p11 (printed 775) gives 'at least 0.33 L' but p11 is an excluded page.

items.question: Under the MUTCD 11th Edition, what is the time limit for work to count as short duration?
items.note: MUTCD 6N.02 P02 D: short duration is work that occupies a location up to 1 hour. NCDOT's MUTCG Chapter 5 (5.2.4, image page) defines short duration as up to 30 minutes; the question names the MUTCD.

items.question: How does NCDOT's MUTCG (Chapter 5, utility and maintenance operations) define short duration work?
items.note: MUTCG Ch. 5, 5.2.4 D - Short Duration (image-only page, folio 76): work that occupies a location up to 30 minutes. Conflicts with MUTCD 6N.02 (up to 1 hour); the question names the MUTCG.

items.question: What minimum cone height does MUTCD Part 6 require on freeways and other high-speed highways?
items.note: MUTCD 6K.02 P01: cones on freeways/high-speed highways or at night: minimum 28 inches; daytime low-speed 18 in. NCDOT Roadway Standard Drawing 1135.01 (Division 11 p47) requires a 36 inch cone on freeways and interstates.

items.question: Which cone size do NCDOT's Division 11 roadway standard drawings require on freeways and interstates?
items.note: Division 11 Combined p47 (rotated drawing, cone details): '36 INCH CONE (REQUIRED FOR FREEWAYS AND INTERSTATES)'; the 28 inch cone is the minimum for all other roads. MUTCD 6K.02 allows 28 in minimum on freeways.

items.question: In NCDOT's MUTCG notes for flashing arrow boards, what minimum mounting height applies to a vehicle-mounted arrow board?
items.note: MUTCG Ch. 2, E. Notes for Flashing Arrow Boards (image page, folio 40) note 2: minimum mounting height of 7 feet for all arrow boards (trailer or vehicle mounted). MUTCD 6L.06 says vehicle-mounted boards should be as high as practicable instead; the question names the MUTCG.

items.question: Under MUTCD Part 6, how high should a vehicle-mounted arrow board be mounted?
items.note: MUTCD 6L.06 P09: minimum mounting height 7 ft, except vehicle-mounted arrow boards, which should be as high as practicable. NCDOT MUTCG Ch. 2 note 2 requires 7 ft for vehicle-mounted boards too.

items.question: When the 2004 work zone rule was finalized, what wording replaced 'pre-existing roadside safety features' in the TTC plan provision of 630.1012(b)(1)?
items.note: 69 FR 54567 (three-column page), FHWA response on 630.1012(b)(1): the proposed term 'pre-existing roadside safety features' changed to 'pre-existing roadside safety hardware' (current CFR 630.1012(b)(1), p10, also says hardware).

items.question: In the Time Table for Evaluating Activity Significance, when do Raleigh Let Division Activities get evaluated?
items.note: NCDOT WZ Safety & Mobility Guidelines Table 2 (title listed in the contents on p2): the only check in the Raleigh Let Division Activities column is 'Six (6) months before Let'. Gold is the table page, not the contents.

items.question: Responsible Charge for Exception Requests: for a state funded Division activity, who requests the exception and who approves it?
items.note: Guidelines Table 4 Responsible Charge for Exception Requests, row State Funded Division Activities: requested by the Project Manager to the Division Engineer for review and approval.

items.question: TMP Implementation Costs: why does FHWA's TMP guide say these costs should be in the overall project cost?
items.note: trans_mgmt_plans 3.10 TMP Implementation Costs (heading listed in the contents, p9): critical because it may be difficult to obtain additional funding at a later time; avoids under-allocation of funds.

items.question: TMP Design Manual 4.1 CADD: what size are full size traffic control plan sheets?
items.note: TMP Part 3 Ch. 4, 4.1 CADD, Scales: full size plan sheets 22" x 34" with a 3" border on the left; half size 11" x 17". Heading listed in the manual's contents.

items.question: Meeting Responsibility: how soon after a project meeting must the TMP plan developer submit draft minutes?
items.note: TMP Part 3 Ch. 7, 7.1 Meeting Responsibility: draft minutes for approval within 3 business days following the meeting. Heading listed in the manual's contents.

items.question: The Standard Specifications let us cover excavated areas with metal plates where the speed is 45 mph or less, so we can plate a trench on a 45 mph road overnight, right?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf

items.note: Standard Specifications 1101-6: metal plates may be used in low speed areas (35 mph or less). The premise (45 mph) is wrong; a 45 mph road does not qualify.

items.question: Under the Standard Specifications, once we're notified of a traffic control safety issue that isn't an imminent danger we have 72 hours to fix it. Is that right?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf

items.note: Standard Specifications 1101-11: remedial action immediately for imminent danger, within 48 hours after notification for a non-imminent safety issue. (The 2023 process review's 72 hours is a smart work zone device repair clause in one contract, not this rule.)

items.question: NCDOT requires high visibility devices on interstate and freeway projects that last 12 months or more. What do those devices include?
items.note: 2023 Process Review: high visibility devices (all new drums and stationary/portable signs with fluorescent post reflector strips) are required on interstate/freeway projects with durations of 24 months or more, not 12. The answer must correct the duration.

items.question: The MUTCG says flaggers have to be rotated every hour. What does it say about alternating traffic under heavy volumes?
items.note: MUTCG Ch. 2 flagging notes (image page, folio 9): rotate flaggers every 2 to 3 hours (not every hour); alternate traffic flow every 2 to 3 minutes under heavy traffic.

items.question: The League of Municipalities work zone card that NCDOT accepts for small-town employees is only good for 2 years before renewal, correct?
items.note: NCDOT Final Rule Implementation, local governments: the League of Municipalities certification is in effect for 4 years, then the employee must renew the card.

items.question: What's the minimum height for traffic cones in a work zone under MUTCD Part 6?
items.note: Missing variable: road speed / time of day. MUTCD 6K.02: daytime and low-speed roads 18 in minimum; freeways, other high-speed highways and at night 28 in minimum.

items.question: How often do the UNEVEN LANES signs have to be repeated where we leave a drop-off of an inch and a half or less in the travel lanes?
items.note: Missing variable: posted speed. TMP 2.4 A): W8-11 every half mile where posted speed < 45 mph, every mile where >= 45 mph.

items.question: What score do you need on the written test to pass an NCDOT-approved work zone qualification course?
items.note: Missing variable: which course. NCDOT Final Rule Implementation: Flagger and Installer courses 70 or better (p3); Work Zone Designer course 80 or better (p5); the Supervisor course gives no grade.

items.question: What cone size do NCDOT's roadway standard drawings call for in a work zone?
items.note: Missing variable: road class. Division 11 p47 (rotated drawing): 36 inch cone required for freeways and interstates; 28 inch cone is the minimum for all other roads.

items.question: What minimum legibility distance does MUTCD Figure 6L-3 give for a Type E arrow board?
items.note: Figure 6L-3 (part6 p70) lists arrow board types A to D only; a cell beyond the table's range. Checked: no 'Type E' arrow board in any wztc document.

items.question: How many work zone records did NCDOT's WZ-EVA database hold by the end of 2025?
items.note: The 2023 process review gives just over 30,000 records as of 11/30/23 only. Checked: no WZ-EVA count for 2024 or 2025 in any wztc document.

items.question: What dollar amount of liquidated damages did NCDOT put in the I-3306 contract for smart work zone devices not repaired within 72 hours?
items.note: 2023 process review p6 says liquidated damages were added for devices not repaired within 72 hours but gives no amount. Checked: no dollar figure near 'I-3306' in any wztc document.

items.question: What passing grade does the written test for NCDOT's Qualified Work Zone Supervisor course require?
items.note: NCDOT Final Rule Implementation p4 requires passing a written test plus two years of OJT but gives no grade (the Flagger/Installer 70 and Designer 80 grades do not apply). Checked: no 'passing grade' near 'Supervisor'.

items.question: What does Hawaii DOT require for flagger certification?
items.note: Another state's rule. Checked: no Hawaii flagger provisions in any wztc document (Hawaii appears only in a payload table of the road user cost guide).

items.question: How many hours of vacation leave do NCDOT employees earn each month?
items.note: Another topic entirely (HR). Checked: no vacation leave text in any wztc document.

items.question: How do I renew a North Carolina commercial driver's license?
items.note: Another topic entirely (DMV licensing). Checked: no 'commercial driver's license' or 'CDL' in any wztc document.

items.question: In FHWA's TMP strategy matrix (Table B.1), what are the triggers for considering lighting devices?
items.note: trans_mgmt_plans Table B.1 TMP Strategy Matrix (continued), Appendix B-8, row IB8 Lighting devices: triggers when night work is being conducted, long project duration, high traffic volume. The table runs over several appendix pages; this row is on a continuation page.

items.question: In Table B.1 of FHWA's TMP guide, when should pedestrian/bicycle access improvements be considered?
items.note: Table B.1 (continued), Appendix B-6, row IA12: long project duration; significant pedestrian/bicyclist activities; existing sidewalks traverse the work zone; a school route traverses the work zone.

items.question: Per the footnote to the traffic control devices part of FHWA's TMP strategy matrix, which category are temporary traffic barriers and crash cushions put in?
items.note: Table B.1, Appendix B-6, footnote 3 on 'B. Traffic Control Devices': other safety devices from MUTCD Part 6 such as temporary traffic barriers and crash cushions are included in the Work Zone Safety Management Strategies category.

items.question: In FHWA's TMP guide Table 5.1 (resources for examples and best practices), what date is listed for Wisconsin DOT's Facilities Development Manual?
items.note: Table 5.1 Resources for Examples and Best Practices (continued), printed 5-14: Wisconsin Department of Transportation, Facilities Development Manual, February 2003. The table runs from 5-10 to 5-14.

items.question: Who are the authors listed on the technical report documentation page of FHWA's Developing and Implementing TMPs for Work Zones guide?
items.note: trans_mgmt_plans Form DOT F 1700.7 (technical report documentation page), field 7 Author(s): Krista Jeannotte and Andre Chandra - Cambridge Systematics. No printed folio.

items.question: What report date is on the technical report documentation form of FHWA's Work Zone ITS Implementation Guide?
items.note: fhwahop14008 technical report documentation page, field 5 Report Date: January 2014. No printed folio.

items.question: What period does the technical report documentation page of the Work Zone Operations Best Practices Guidebook (third edition) give as covered?
items.note: bpguidebook Form DOT F 1700.7, field 13 Type of Report and Period Covered: 1/23/2008 to 10/30/2013. No printed folio (PDF label 'C').

items.note: 23 CFR 630.1012(e) Responsible persons: designate a trained person, as specified in 630.1008(d).

items.question: For TIP projects and Raleigh Let Division Activities, what do NCDOT's work zone guidelines say to use to determine the level of significance?
items.note: Guidelines p17: use the Criteria chart shown in Table 3 (See page 19); other division activities and encroachments use the procedures on pages 20-21.

items.question: In Table 37 of FHWA's work zone road user cost guide, is highway advisory radio listed as a public awareness or a motorist information strategy?
items.note: fhwahop12005 Table 37 Work zone management strategies by category - public information (page rotated, printed 59): Highway advisory radio is in the Motorist Information column.

items.question: Can thermoplastic pavement markings be applied when the ambient air and pavement temperatures are both exactly 50 degrees F?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf

items.note: Standard Specifications 1205-4(B) Thermoplastic weather limitations: ambient air and pavement temperature 50°F or higher (so 50°F exactly is allowed). Near-identical to the polyurea rule on 12-8 (40°F).

items.question: What minimum ambient air and pavement temperature do the Standard Specifications set for applying polyurea pavement markings?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf

items.note: Standard Specifications 1205-5(A) Polyurea weather limitations: 40°F or higher. Near-identical to the thermoplastic rule (50°F, 12-6).

items.question: Our haul trucks will be entering and leaving an open travel lane on a multi-lane, controlled access road. How much below the posted speed limit are they allowed to be when they enter the lane?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf
expected.value: 10 mph below the posted speed limit

items.note: Standard Specifications 1101-7 Hauling Operations: on multi-lane, controlled access roadways haul vehicles shall not enter/exit an open travel lane at speeds more than 10 mph below the posted speed limit; acceleration to within 10 mph only on paved surfaces. Both conditions (multi-lane and controlled access) apply.

items.question: For a permanent pothole patching operation on an interstate with limited shoulder and guardrail, what minimum mounting height from the roadway to a ground-mounted sign does the MUTCG call for?
items.note: MUTCG Ch. 5 Notes on Permanent Pothole Patching on Interstate and Multilane Divided Facilities with Limited Shoulder and Guardrail (image page, folio 110), note 4: minimum five feet for interstates and other high volume roadways, minimum one foot for all other roadways (signs on vehicles: one foot, note 3).

items.question: When an AFAD operation is idle for 30 minutes, how far from the edge line must the AFAD units be moved, per the MUTCG?
items.note: MUTCG Ch. 2, F. Notes for AFAD (image page, folio 42) note 7: when work is not pursued for 30 minutes or longer, all parts of the AFAD unit removed from the travel lane a minimum of 2' from the edge line. 30 minutes exactly triggers it.

items.question: According to FHWA's Work Zone ITS Implementation Guide, by how much can speed monitoring displays reduce speeds?
items.note: fhwahop14008 6.5.2 (printed 60): speed monitoring displays could reduce speeds by 4-6 mph; one study found a 20 to 40 percent reduction in vehicles going 10+ mph over the limit.

items.question: In FHWA's work zone road user cost guide example, what hourly employment cost (December 2010) is used for the value of business travel time?
items.note: fhwahop12005 Example (printed 15), Step 3: hourly employment cost = $29.75 (December, 2010); value of a person's business travel time = 100% of median hourly wages plus benefits.

items.question: Under FHWA's Work Zone Self Assessment categories, which project type covers recurring mobile work like pothole patching, striping and mowing?
items.note: rule_guide 5.x (printed 5-6), WZSA categories: Type IV - small impact, low public interest, short to moderate duration, usually mobile and recurring (striping, guardrail repair, pothole patching, mowing).

items.question: In the Work Zone Operations Best Practices Guidebook index by roadway characteristics, which practices are listed for toll roads?
items.note: bpguidebook Best Practices by Roadway Characteristics (PDF p20, printed page 6): Toll Roads - C1-1, G4-4, G4-5.

items.question: What are the objectives of work zone impacts assessment during construction, according to FHWA's work zone impacts assessment guide?
items.note: wzi_guide 7.2 (printed 7-2): six objectives - resolve pre-construction coordination issues; assess proposed changes before work starts; implement the TMP; actively monitor and manage impacts; revise the TMP; document findings or lessons.

items.question: Per Standard Specifications Table 1205-5, what minimum reflectivity must yellow Type 3 wet reflective high performance tape meet when measured wet?

expected.source: 2024 Standard Specifications for Roads and Structures.pdf

items.note: Table 1205-5 Reflectometer Requirements for Cold Applied Plastic Tape: each Type label is a merged cell over a White and a Yellow row; Type 3 (Wet): white 250, yellow 200 mcd/lux/m2 (Type 3 Dry: 500/300).

items.question: In Table 21 of FHWA's work zone road user cost guide, which price index is used to update depreciation costs for truck trailers?
items.note: fhwahop12005 Table 21 Price adjustments for VOC components (printed 35): the index name is a merged cell spanning all vehicle columns; Depreciation -> Producer Price Index - Commodity Data Transportation Equipment (14); truck trailers item code 1406.

items.question: In the RealCost delay table of Example 2.2 in FHWA's road user cost guide, the queuing delay for 08-09 is 23.81. In what units?
items.note: fhwahop12005 Example 2.2 table (printed 9), footnote (**): delay times reported as average delay time per vehicle in minutes. The table itself has no unit.
